name: CAPC Musée d Art Contemporain
funding: €3.8M. Ville de Bordeaux, DRAC Nouvelle-Aquitaine, les Amis du CAPC.

name: Kunsthaus Bregenz
funding: Commissioned by the State of Vorarlberg. Principal sponsor Hypo Vorarlberg; also illwerke vkw, Zumtobel, UNIQA (2026), Hugo Boss and Mader Flatz Schett.
watch: State museum of Vorarlberg designed by Peter Zumthor.
why_flagged: illwerke vkw is state-owned and mostly hydro but also sells natural gas, so B under the utility rule.
records_note: Names its main sponsors in text and others as logos, with no date; it posts no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Kunsthalle Bremen
funding: Run by the Kunstverein in Bremen. Funders include Senator für Kultur, Senatskanzlei, Sparkasse Bremen, EY, Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung, Fritz Thyssen Stiftung, Hollweg Stiftung and Kaefer.
watch: Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung was set up in 1988 by the son of cigarette maker Hermann F. Reemtsma, so its money is tobacco-family money.
records_note: The Kunsthalle shows 22 funders as undated logos and publishes no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Institute of Modern Art
funding: Arts Queensland and Creative Australia. Partners include Sullivan+Strumpf, The Calile Hotel, Coopers, Bird in Hand, Autex and Creative Brisbane Collab.
watch: Oldest independent contemporary art center in Australia (Brisbane, est. 1975).
records_note: Names its board, shows funders and partners as undated logos, and links no annual reports or accounts from its site.

name: Arnolfini
funding: Arts Council England, Bristol City Council and UWE Bristol, which owns Bush House and leases the gallery space back. Ashley Clinton and Barker-Mill Trust is also credited.
records_note: Names its eleven trustees but shows funder logos only, undated, and posts no annual reports; accounts for 2020 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: Wiels Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Flemish, French-speaking, Brussels and VGC governments. Structural partners: Duvel Moortgat, Phillips, Aureus Ars & Scientia. Exhibition partners include Loterie Nationale and Gulbenkian France; GBL supports education.
watch: Independent non-profit operating on regional cultural subventions.
why_flagged: Flemish, French-speaking, Brussels and VGC governments. Structural partners: Duvel Moortgat, Phillips, Aureus Ars & Scientia. Exhibition partners include Loterie Nationale and Gulbenkian France; GBL supports education.
records_note: WIELS files accounts with the National Bank of Belgium, names its board and general assembly, and lists partners by name without a date.

name: Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires (MALBA)
funding: Fundación Costantini, ICBC, Citi, corporate circles.
watch: Private foundation museum with banking and multinational sponsorships.
why_flagged: Fundación Malba, set up by Eduardo Costantini, runs it. Its 2024 audited accounts show founder gifts at 12 percent of income, presenting partners and sponsors 58 percent and own earnings 17 percent, with a surplus. Collaborators on its sponsors page include Chevron, Bloomberg, Zurich and Telecom.
records_note: It posts financial statements for 2005 to 2024 but no annual report; sponsors show only as logos and no board members are named.

name: Contemporary Calgary
funding: Individual Leadership Circle and lifetime donors. LOOK gala presented by Mawer (2025), Rogers (2023) and National Bank (2020 to 2022); Holt Renfrew sponsors the dinner.
watch: Housed in the historic Centennial Planetarium.
records_note: Posts a 2024-25 annual report, names its Leadership Circle donors undated and lists sixteen board members; accounts were not checked.

name: Kettle's Yard
funding: University of Cambridge gallery. Arts Council England, Research England, Cambridge City Council; corporate supporters include David Zwirner, Emmanuel College, Murray Edwards College, City Asset and Resolute AV.
watch: Retains Jim Ede's founding vision of intimate, unbranded domestic galleries.
records_note: Annual reports 2009-10 to 2024-25 are online with a 2024/25 supporters list; parent University of Cambridge publishes accounts; a committee is listed.

name: National Gallery of Australia
funding: Commonwealth statutory body. 2024-25 major partners: Qantas Airways and Pallion; Wesfarmers Arts is First Nations Arts Partner. Mazda backed the 2024 Gauguin show.
why_flagged: Commonwealth statutory body. 2024-25 major partners: Qantas Airways and Pallion; Wesfarmers Arts is First Nations Arts Partner. Mazda backed the 2024 Gauguin show.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports for 2022-23 to 2024-25 with audited accounts and Council names, plus an undated named partner list.

name: Norval Foundation
funding: Property investor Louis Norval financed it entirely at the 2018 opening and set up a capital fund. Sponsors include Schroders (art prize), Stonehage Fleming (2021 auction) and Sanlam.
watch: Centre for art and cultural expression in Steenberg, Cape Town. Custodian of the Gerard Sekoto Foundation; funded through philanthropic endowment dedicated to African modern and contemporary art.
records_note: It names its twelve trustees on the About page but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: Zeitz MOCAA
funding: Jochen Zeitz donated the collection he had loaned; sponsors include Gucci and BMW, the Mellon Foundation funds fellowships, and the board now pays.
watch: Corporate Underwritten: Public-private partnership in Cape Town's Grain Silo complex. Major funding from German business executive Jochen Zeitz (Puma/Kering) and South African commercial real estate REITs; independent board of trustees.
records_note: Its supporters page names corporate members, founders and sponsors including the Mellon Foundation and BMW, undated, but it posts no reports, accounts or board.
